```{r}
has_shared_birthday <- function(group_size) {
  birthdays <- sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

birthday_results <- tibble::tibble(
  group_size = 2:50,
  probability = purrr::map_dbl(
    group_size,
    function(n) mean(replicate(10000, has_shared_birthday(n)))
  )
)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(birthday_results, aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a shared birthday",
    x = "Number of people in the group",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

dplyr::filter(birthday_results, group_size %in% c(23, 50))
```

The estimated probability that at least two people share a birthday increases with group size. It reaches 50.7% with just 23 people and rises to 97.1% with 50 people.

## Problem 2

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

subject_files <- tibble(
  file_path = list.files(
    "data",
    pattern = "^(con|exp)_[0-9]+\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    recursive = TRUE
  )
)

if (nrow(subject_files) != 20) {
  stop("Expected 20 participant CSVs in the data folder next to the Rmd.")
}

subject_files <- subject_files |>
  mutate(
    weekly_data = purrr::map(file_path, read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
  )

study_data <- subject_files |>
  mutate(
    file_name = basename(file_path),
    arm = if_else(str_starts(file_name, "con_"), "Control", "Experimental"),
    subject_id = str_extract(file_name, "[0-9]+")
  ) |>
  select(subject_id, arm, weekly_data) |>
  unnest(weekly_data) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(subject_id, arm),
    names_to = "week",
    names_transform = list(week = readr::parse_number),
    values_to = "observation"
  )

head(study_data)
```

```{r}
ggplot(study_data, aes(x = week, y = observation, group = subject_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(study_data$week))) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly observations by study arm",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

Observations in the control arm fluctuated from week to week with no clear overall trend. In the experimental arm, observations generally increased over time, and the difference between the two groups was most apparent in weeks 7 and 8.

## Problem3
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(123)

simulate_t_test <- function(true_mu) {
  sample_data <- rnorm(n = 30, mean = true_mu, sd = 5)

  t.test(sample_data, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided") |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}

simulation_results <- expand_grid(
  true_mu = 0:6,
  iteration = seq_len(5000)
) |>
  mutate(
    test_result = purrr::map(true_mu, simulate_t_test)
  ) |>
  unnest(test_result) |>
  mutate(rejected = p.value < 0.05)

simulation_summary <- simulation_results |>
  group_by(true_mu) |>
  summarize(
    rejection_rate = mean(rejected),
    mean_all = mean(estimate),
    mean_rejected = mean(estimate[rejected]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

simulation_summary
```

```{r}
ggplot(simulation_summary, aes(x = true_mu, y = rejection_rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Rejection rate of the one-sample t-test",
    x = "True mean",
    y = "Proportion of tests rejecting the null"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
estimate_plot_data <- simulation_summary |>
  select(true_mu, mean_all, mean_rejected) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_all, mean_rejected),
    names_to = "sample_set",
    values_to = "average_estimate"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    sample_set = recode(
      sample_set,
      mean_all = "All samples",
      mean_rejected = "Samples rejecting the null"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  estimate_plot_data,
  aes(x = true_mu, y = average_estimate, color = sample_set)
) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(
    title = "Average estimated mean by true mean",
    x = "True mean",
    y = "Average estimated mean",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Across all samples, the average estimated mean is close to the true mean. In samples where the null hypothesis is rejected, for small positive effects, the average estimate tends to be higher than the true mean because samples with unusually large estimates are more likely to reach significance. As statistical power approaches 100%, this difference narrows. When the true mean is zero, two-sided tests select extreme estimates in both directions, so their average remains close to zero.
